instruction: Look up Iron and Stella's email addresses in the tuition payment spreadsheet and add them to the email's receiver field.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened tuition_payment.xlsx, misread 2 of 4 unpaid students (typed john and sophia instead of iron and stella), added emails to To field, then spent remaining turns stuck on network save dialog.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open files from file manager, read spreadsheet data, switch between windows, type email addresses into Thunderbird compose To field, interact with Thunderbird dialogs.
metadata.failure_analysis: Model hallucinated spreadsheet data - correctly identified fox and nancy as unpaid but incorrectly added john and sophia (who had 'Yes') instead of iron and stella. Then wasted ~20 turns waiting for stuck network save.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified version of original task: instead of finding all 4 unpaid students, the instruction names exactly 2 students (Iron and Stella) to look up. This reduces the cognitive load of scanning the entire spreadsheet while still requiring cross-app data lookup.
metadata.explanation: Task requires looking up Iron and Stella in tuition_payment.xlsx (rows 10 and 20), finding their emails (iron@someuniversity.edu, stella@someuniversity.edu), and adding them to Thunderbird To field. Evaluator checks accessibility tree for address pills. Partial credit: 0.5 per email.

scoring_breakdown.add_iron_email: 0.5 - iron@someuniversity.edu appears as address pill in To field
scoring_breakdown.add_stella_email: 0.5 - stella@someuniversity.edu appears as address pill in To field

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses accessibility tree getter and check_accessibility_tree metric to verify Thunderbird compose To field contains the expected email addresses.
CSS selectors properly target address-pill labels within the MsgHeadersToolbar To field, using substring match (name*=) for iron@someuniversity.edu and stella@someuniversity.edu.
Both emails required by the instruction are checked - complete coverage of verification requirements.
Expected email addresses match the task description and spreadsheet data referenced in the config.

Minor issue: metadata claims partial credit (0.5 per email) but check_accessibility_tree returns 0.0 immediately if any rule's selector finds no elements (line 253), so no partial credit is actually possible. This is a scoring granularity issue, not a correctness issue.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To support partial credit as described in metadata, consider splitting into two separate evaluator entries or using a custom metric that awards 0.5 per matched selector rule instead of the multiplicative scoring in check_accessibility_tree.
